title: Uninformed search
focus: A search problem needs a state, legal successor actions, a start, a goal test and a path cost.

weeks.label: Unit 1
weeks.expectedWork: Original attempt, exposition, three problems, separate corrections, topic evidence and delayed reassessment. 90-minute relative unit; no assigned date.
inlineQuestions: AI01-Q1: On that graph, list the UCS pop order and the final goal cost. Explain why stopping when G is first generated would be wrong.
AI01-Q2: A finite directed graph has a reachable cycle. Can DFS without a visited set run forever? What changes with a visited set?
AI01-Q3: For a full binary search tree with root at depth 0 and every goal at depth 3, how many nodes does BFS pop before its first goal, assuming it tests goals on pop?

gradingKeys.AI01-Q1: S, A, G; cost 2. The first generated G has cost 5 but a cheaper frontier route remains.
gradingKeys.AI01-Q2: Yes, an unfortunate successor order may loop forever. Graph DFS with a visited set examines finitely many states/edges and terminates; it still need not find a shortest path.
gradingKeys.AI01-Q3: All 1+2+4 nodes at smaller depths, then the first depth-three node: 8 pops. Distinguish nodes generated from nodes popped.

title: Informed search: greedy and A*
focus: A heuristic h estimates remaining goal cost.

weeks.label: Unit 2
weeks.expectedWork: Original attempt, exposition, three problems, separate corrections, topic evidence and delayed reassessment. 90-minute relative unit; no assigned date.
inlineQuestions: AI02-Q1: Trace greedy and A* on the worked graph, testing the goal on pop. Give the returned path cost for each.
AI02-Q2: On the same graph, is h(S)=4, h(A)=1, h(G)=0 admissible? Is it consistent? Check each edge.
AI02-Q3: What does A* become when h is identically zero? Why is a heuristic with h(A)=10 invalid for the optimality guarantee here?

gradingKeys.AI02-Q1: Greedy: S,G, cost 7. A*: S,A,G, cost 4.
gradingKeys.AI02-Q2: Admissible: true remaining costs are 4,2,0. Inconsistent on S→A because 4 > 2+1. Other edges satisfy consistency.
gradingKeys.AI02-Q3: It becomes UCS. Since true remaining cost from A is 2, h(A)=10 overestimates and is not admissible.

title: Adversarial search: minimax and alpha–beta
focus: In a deterministic two-player zero-sum game tree, a MAX node chooses the largest child value and a MIN node chooses the smallest.

weeks.label: Unit 3
weeks.expectedWork: Original attempt, exposition, three problems, separate corrections, topic evidence and delayed reassessment. 90-minute relative unit; no assigned date.
inlineQuestions: AI03-Q1: Complete minimax when L has leaves 3,5 and R has leaves 2,9. Which branch is chosen?
AI03-Q2: Trace left-to-right alpha–beta on that tree. Which leaf is not examined and why?
AI03-Q3: Reverse the two leaves under R to 9,2. Does the value change? Does that pruning still happen?

gradingKeys.AI03-Q1: L returns 3; R returns 2; root chooses L with value 3.
gradingKeys.AI03-Q2: The leaf 9 under R is pruned. R already has beta 2 while root alpha is 3, so it cannot beat L.
gradingKeys.AI03-Q3: The value stays 3. Seeing 9 first does not allow the cutoff; both R leaves must be examined in this order.

title: Propositional and predicate logic
focus: A proposition has a truth value; an interpretation assigns values to atomic propositions.

weeks.label: Unit 4
weeks.expectedWork: Original attempt, exposition, three problems, separate corrections, topic evidence and delayed reassessment. 90-minute relative unit; no assigned date.
inlineQuestions: AI04-Q1: Does P→Q together with ¬Q entail ¬P? Prove it by eliminating the possibility P=true.
AI04-Q2: Give a domain and a relation showing ∀x∃y R(x,y) does not entail ∃y∀x R(x,y).
AI04-Q3: Resolve the clauses (¬P∨Q) and (P∨R) on P. Does the resolvent alone imply both original clauses?

gradingKeys.AI04-Q1: Yes. If P were true, the implication would force Q true, contradicting ¬Q. This is modus tollens.
gradingKeys.AI04-Q2: Domain {1,2}; R(x,y) means x=y. Each x has its own witness, but neither single y equals every x.
gradingKeys.AI04-Q3: Resolvent Q∨R. No: P=true,Q=false,R=true satisfies Q∨R but falsifies ¬P∨Q.

title: Conditional independence and Bayesian networks
focus: A Bayesian network is a directed acyclic graph with one conditional probability table per node.

weeks.label: Unit 5
weeks.expectedWork: Original attempt, exposition, three problems, separate corrections, topic evidence and delayed reassessment. 90-minute relative unit; no assigned date.
inlineQuestions: AI05-Q1: Factor the joint for A→B→C. What conditional independence is guaranteed?
AI05-Q2: For A→C←B, compare conditioning on nothing, on C, and on a child D of C.
AI05-Q3: A is binary and B is binary with parent A. How many free scalar probabilities specify P(A) and P(B|A)?

gradingKeys.AI05-Q1: P(A,B,C)=P(A)P(B|A)P(C|B); A is independent of C conditional on B.
gradingKeys.AI05-Q2: The collider path is blocked without evidence; observing C or its descendant D activates it. A and B are marginally independent in this graph but conditional independence is not guaranteed after those observations.
gradingKeys.AI05-Q3: One for the Bernoulli root A, and one for each of B’s two parent configurations: total 3.

title: Exact inference through variable elimination
focus: To compute a posterior, first substitute observed evidence into the factors.

weeks.label: Unit 6
weeks.expectedWork: Original attempt, exposition, three problems, separate corrections, topic evidence and delayed reassessment. 90-minute relative unit; no assigned date.
inlineQuestions: AI06-Q1: Compute P(B=1) and P(A=0|B=1) in the example. Show the sum and the normalization.
AI06-Q2: For A→B→C with evidence C=c, write the unnormalized factor for query A after eliminating hidden B.
AI06-Q3: Factors f(X,Y), g(Y,Z), h(Z) are present, all variables binary. Eliminate Y first. Name the intermediate scope and its table size.

gradingKeys.AI06-Q2: f(A)=P(A) Σ_b P(b|A)P(c|b). Normalize f(A) over A to obtain the posterior.
gradingKeys.AI06-Q3: Multiply f and g to form scope {X,Y,Z} with 8 entries; sum Y out to produce a factor on {X,Z} with 4 entries. h(Z) need not be included until needed.

title: Approximate inference through sampling
focus: Forward sampling draws each node given its already sampled parents.

weeks.label: Unit 7
weeks.expectedWork: Original attempt, exposition, three problems, separate corrections, topic evidence and delayed reassessment. 90-minute relative unit; no assigned date.
inlineQuestions: AI07-Q1: Evidence occurs with probability 0.01. Out of 10,000 independent forward samples, what is the expected number accepted by rejection sampling? Is it guaranteed?
AI07-Q2: Likelihood-weighted samples have A values 1,0,0 and corresponding weights 0.8,0.1,0.1. Estimate P(A=1|B=1).
AI07-Q3: In A→B→C with B fixed as evidence, should a Gibbs update resample B? What determines an update to A?

gradingKeys.AI07-Q1: Expected count 10000×0.01=100, not a guarantee; the count is random.
gradingKeys.AI07-Q2: Weighted query total 0.8 divided by total weight 1.0 gives 0.8. Finite-sample estimates vary from the exact posterior.
gradingKeys.AI07-Q3: B remains fixed. The distribution for A is proportional to P(A)P(B|A), using its Markov blanket. Normalize before drawing.
